model_annotation: Figure 2 is a horizontal bar chart titled "Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data." The chart compares the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens generated by the Mistral-v0.2 base model and its fine-tuned variants across six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis lists these specialties, arranged in the same order as in the table above. The horizontal axis represents "Negative log-probability," with a linear scale ranging from approximately 27 to 32, marked at intervals of 1 unit (27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32). Each specialty has two adjacent horizontal bars: the left bar (lighter orange) represents the base Mistral-v0.2 model, and the right bar (darker orange) represents the same model fine-tuned on that specialty’s data. The legend at the top of the chart confirms this color coding: “Mistral-v0.2-Base” (lighter orange) and “Fine-tuned on” (darker orange), with each specialty listed beneath. For all specialties, the fine-tuned model’s bar is shorter than the base model’s bar, indicating lower negative log-probabilities (i.e., higher likelihoods) for the relevant tokens. The most pronounced reduction is seen in the "Infect" specialty, where the base model’s bar extends to approximately 31.0 and the fine-tuned bar drops to about 28.5. In contrast, the "Cardio" specialty shows a smaller improvement, with the base model at about 30.5 and the fine-tuned model at around 29.5. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning reduces negative log-probabilities across all specialties, suggesting improved alignment with clinical terminology specific to each domain.
